question: Create a Manhattan plot from GWAS summary statistics. Plot -log10(p-value) against genomic position, grouped by chromosome. Highlight genome-wide significant SNPs (p < 5x10^-8) in red.

files.eval_guideline: Manhattan plot must show -log10(p-value) vs chromosomal position with SNPs grouped by chromosome and a genome-wide significance threshold (p < 5e-8) visually marked; chromosome colors, significance-SNP marking style, and font may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename manhattan_plot.png and inferred PNG image format. The candidate clearly corresponds to the requested Manhattan plot from the GWAS summary statistics.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual agreement on -log10(p-value) versus genomic position, chromosome grouping, and marking genome-wide significance at p < 5e-8, while allowing styling differences. Semantic comparison evaluates these plot features without requiring pixel-level identity.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show Manhattan plots of GWAS summary statistics, with genomic position grouped by chromosomes 1–22 on the horizontal axis and -log10(p-value) on the vertical axis. Both display six prominent association peaks on chromosomes 1, 2, 6, 9, 14, and 16, reaching approximately 11–11.6, with closely matching background and isolated SNP patterns. Both highlight genome-wide significant SNPs in red and mark the p < 5×10^-8 threshold at approximately 7.3. Both also show a suggestive threshold at 5. The candidate uses alternating blue chromosome colors, dashed or dotted threshold lines, and larger significant markers; these are cosmetic differences. It additionally labels lead SNPs, displays all chromosome numbers, and reports 19,998 SNPs and 199 significant SNPs, information not explicitly stated in the reference. Exact counts cannot be independently verified visually, but no substantive discrepancy is apparent. The scientific message and required plotting elements are equivalent.
